claim: The yeast centrosome is called the spindle pole body (SPB).
source: Duplication of the yeast centrosome (called the spindle pole body, SPB) is thought to occur through a series of discrete steps that culminate in insertion of the new SPB into the nuclear envelope (NE).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a definitional statement.

claim: SPB duplication culminates in insertion of the new SPB into the nuclear envelope.
source: Duplication of the yeast centrosome (called the spindle pole body, SPB) is thought to occur through a series of discrete steps that culminate in insertion of the new SPB into the nuclear envelope (NE).
evidence: This is stated as a known aspect of SPB duplication in the abstract.

claim: A novel two-color structured illumination microscopy with single-particle averaging (SPA-SIM) approach was developed to study SPB component localization during duplication.
source: To better understand this process, we developed a novel two-color structured illumination microscopy with single-particle averaging (SPA-SIM) approach to study the localization of all 18 SPB components during duplication using endogenously expressed fluorescent protein derivatives.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the development of this method.

claim: All 18 SPB components were studied during duplication using endogenously expressed fluorescent protein derivatives.
source: To better understand this process, we developed a novel two-color structured illumination microscopy with single-particle averaging (SPA-SIM) approach to study the localization of all 18 SPB components during duplication using endogenously expressed fluorescent protein derivatives.
evidence: The abstract states that all 18 SPB components were examined.

claim: SPB duplication begins by formation of an asymmetric Sfi1 filament at mitotic exit.
source: The increased resolution and quantitative intensity information obtained using this method allowed us to demonstrate that SPB duplication begins by formation of an asymmetric Sfi1 filament at mitotic exit followed by Mps1-dependent assembly of a Spc29- and Spc42-dependent complex at its tip.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the SPA-SIM data.

claim: Mps1-dependent assembly of a Spc29- and Spc42-dependent complex occurs at the tip of the Sfi1 filament.
source: The increased resolution and quantitative intensity information obtained using this method allowed us to demonstrate that SPB duplication begins by formation of an asymmetric Sfi1 filament at mitotic exit followed by Mps1-dependent assembly of a Spc29- and Spc42-dependent complex at its tip.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Proteins involved in membrane insertion (Mps2, Bbp1, and Ndc1) accumulate at the new SPB early in duplication.
source: Our observation that proteins involved in membrane insertion, such as Mps2, Bbp1, and Ndc1, also accumulate at the new SPB early in duplication suggests that SPB assembly and NE insertion are coupled events during SPB formation in wild-type cells.
evidence: This is a primary observation stated in the abstract.

claim: SPB assembly and NE insertion are coupled events during SPB formation in wild-type cells.
source: Our observation that proteins involved in membrane insertion, such as Mps2, Bbp1, and Ndc1, also accumulate at the new SPB early in duplication suggests that SPB assembly and NE insertion are coupled events during SPB formation in wild-type cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the abstract.

claim: MTOCs perform functions including cell signaling, cilia assembly, intraflagellar transport, and chromosome segregation.
source: MTOCs perform a variety of functions in the cell, including cell signaling, cilia assembly, intraflagellar transport, and chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Duplication of centrosomes and SPBs once per cell cycle is essential to facilitate the formation of a bipolar spindle.
source: Duplication of a class of MTOCs known as centrosomes (in metazoans) or spindle pole bodies (SPBs, in fungi) once per cell cycle is essential to facilitate the formation of a bipolar spindle (Winey and O'Toole, 2001; Winey and Bloom, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Defects in centrosome duplication are linked to cancer and other diseases.
source: Defects in centrosome duplication are linked to cancer and other diseases (Chavali et al., 2014; Godinho and Pellman, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The SPB of Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the best characterized MTOC both cytologically and molecularly.
source: Perhaps the best characterized MTOC both cytologically and molecularly is the SPB of Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence: This is stated as a comparative assessment in the introduction.

claim: The SPB is a multilayered cylindrical organelle embedded in the nuclear envelope throughout the yeast lifecycle.
source: Electron microscopy (EM) studies show that the SPB is a multilayered cylindrical organelle that is embedded in the nuclear envelope (NE) throughout the yeast lifecycle (Byers and Goetsch, 1974, 1975).
evidence: This is stated with supporting EM citations.

claim: The outer and inner plaques of the SPB nucleate cytoplasmic and nuclear microtubules, respectively.
source: The outer and inner plaques of the SPB nucleate cytoplasmic and nuclear microtubules, respectively, while the central plaque is key to the structural integrity of the SPB and anchorage of the SPB to the NE via hook-like appendages visible by electron tomography (O'Toole et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The central plaque is key to the structural integrity of the SPB and anchorage of the SPB to the NE via hook-like appendages.
source: The outer and inner plaques of the SPB nucleate cytoplasmic and nuclear microtubules, respectively, while the central plaque is key to the structural integrity of the SPB and anchorage of the SPB to the NE via hook-like appendages visible by electron tomography (O'Toole et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citation.

claim: The half-bridge is a modified region of the NE associated with one side of the SPB.
source: Associated with one side of the SPB is a modified region of the NE known as the half-bridge, which is important for SPB duplication and cytoplasmic microtubule formation during G1 phase and mating (Byers and Goetsch, 1974, 1975; Knop and Schiebel, 1998).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The half-bridge is important for SPB duplication and cytoplasmic microtubule formation during G1 phase and mating.
source: Associated with one side of the SPB is a modified region of the NE known as the half-bridge, which is important for SPB duplication and cytoplasmic microtubule formation during G1 phase and mating (Byers and Goetsch, 1974, 1975; Knop and Schiebel, 1998).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: SPBs and centrosomes share a number of components including proteins involved in duplication, structure, microtubule nucleation, regulators, and assembly principles.
source: Although SPBs and centrosomes are morphologically distinct, they share a number of components, including proteins involved in duplication (Sfi1 and Cdc31/centrin), structure (Spc110/pericentrin and Nud1/centriolin), microtubule nucleation (γ-tubulin complex, composed of Tub4, Spc97, and Spc98 in budding yeast), regulators (Mps1 and cyclin-dependent kinases; Cdks), and assembly principles (Jaspersen and Winey, 2004; Kollman et al., 2011; Winey and Bloom, 2012; Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Analysis of SPB duplication in yeast has provided key mechanistic and regulatory insights into the control of centrosome duplication in higher eukaryotes.
source: Analysis of SPB duplication in yeast has provided key mechanistic and regulatory insights into the control of centrosome duplication in higher eukaryotes (Fu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: Formation of a new SPB occurs adjacent to the mother SPB.
source: Formation of a new SPB occurs adjacent to the mother SPB.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: SPB duplication is typically broken down into three steps based on cytological examination of wild-type and mutant yeast cells.
source: Duplication is typically broken down into three steps based on cytological examination of wild-type and mutant yeast cells (Figure 1A) (Adams and Kilmartin, 2000; Jaspersen and Winey, 2004; Winey and Bloom, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The integral membrane proteins Mps3 and Kar1 localize to the nuclear and cytoplasmic face of the half-bridge, respectively.
source: The integral membrane proteins Mps3 and Kar1 localize to the nuclear and cytoplasmic face of the half-bridge, respectively, and likely serve as structural components that are involved in the localization of Sfi1 and Cdc31 (Vallen et al., 1992a, 1994; Spang et al., 1995; Jaspersen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Mps3 and Kar1 likely serve as structural components involved in the localization of Sfi1 and Cdc31.
source: The integral membrane proteins Mps3 and Kar1 localize to the nuclear and cytoplasmic face of the half-bridge, respectively, and likely serve as structural components that are involved in the localization of Sfi1 and Cdc31 (Vallen et al., 1992a, 1994; Spang et al., 1995; Jaspersen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on cited work.

claim: Sfi1 is a long helical protein that contains multiple binding sites along its length for the yeast centrin, Cdc31.
source: Sfi1 is a long helical protein that contains multiple binding sites along its length for the yeast centrin, Cdc31 (Kilmartin, 2003; Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Dephosphorylation of Cdk1 sites in the C-terminus of Sfi1 initiates elongation of the half-bridge to a full bridge.
source: Dephosphorylation of Cdk1 sites in the C-terminus of Sfi1 initiates elongation of the half-bridge to a full bridge, most likely via oligomerization of C-terminal ends of Sfi1 in an anti-parallel manner that allows free N-termini to associate directly or indirectly with components of the satellite—the new SPB precursor (Avena et al., 2014; Elserafy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Half-bridge elongation most likely occurs via oligomerization of C-terminal ends of Sfi1 in an anti-parallel manner.
source: Dephosphorylation of Cdk1 sites in the C-terminus of Sfi1 initiates elongation of the half-bridge to a full bridge, most likely via oligomerization of C-terminal ends of Sfi1 in an anti-parallel manner that allows free N-termini to associate directly or indirectly with components of the satellite—the new SPB precursor (Avena et al., 2014; Elserafy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a likely mechanism based on cited work.

claim: The satellite is predicted by immunoEM to be composed of four of the 18 SPB components: Spc42, Spc29, Cnm67, and Nud1.
source: ImmunoEM predicts that the satellite is composed of four of the 18 SPB components, Spc42, Spc29, Cnm67, and Nud1 (Adams and Kilmartin, 1999).
evidence: This is stated based on immunoEM data with citation.

claim: Trimers of Spc42 dimers form a hexagonal lattice visible by cryoEM within the mother SPB core.
source: How the satellite assembles is unknown, but within the mother SPB core, trimers of Spc42 dimers form a hexagonal lattice that is visible by cryoEM (Bullitt et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation.

claim: The N-terminus of Spc42 associates with Spc29 and with Spc110.
source: The N-terminus of Spc42 associates with Spc29 and with Spc110, a spacer protein that tethers the γ-tubulin complex to the inner plaque (Elliott et al., 1999; Muller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Spc110 is a spacer protein that tethers the γ-tubulin complex to the inner plaque.
source: The N-terminus of Spc42 associates with Spc29 and with Spc110, a spacer protein that tethers the γ-tubulin complex to the inner plaque (Elliott et al., 1999; Muller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The C-terminus of Spc42 associates with Cnm67.
source: The C-terminus of Spc42 associates with Cnm67, another spacer protein that associates with the signaling scaffold Nud1/centriolin and the outer plaque receptor for the γ-tubulin complex, Spc72 (Knop and Schiebel, 1998; Gruneberg et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Cnm67 is a spacer protein that associates with the signaling scaffold Nud1/centriolin and the outer plaque receptor for the γ-tubulin complex, Spc72.
source: The C-terminus of Spc42 associates with Cnm67, another spacer protein that associates with the signaling scaffold Nud1/centriolin and the outer plaque receptor for the γ-tubulin complex, Spc72 (Knop and Schiebel, 1998; Gruneberg et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Linkage of the SPB to the NE is thought to occur via Spc29, which binds to the soluble protein Bbp1 that in turn associates with the integral membrane protein Mps2.
source: Linkage of the SPB to the NE is thought to occur via Spc29, which binds to the soluble protein Bbp1 that in turn associates with the integral membrane protein Mps2 (Schramm et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as a proposed mechanism with citation.

claim: Mutations in NDC1 and NBP1 result in many of the same phenotypes as BBP1 and MPS2 mutants, including defects in SPB insertion into the NE.
source: For example, mutations in NDC1 and NBP1 result in many of the same phenotypes as BBP1 and MPS2 mutants, including defects in SPB insertion into the NE (Winey et al., 1991; Chial et al., 1998; Schramm et al., 2000; Araki et al., 2006; Kupke et al., 2011; Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Ndc1 and Nbp1 are presumed to anchor the SPB in the NE through unknown binding interactions with the non-membrane core SPB.
source: Therefore, it is presumed that Ndc1 and Nbp1 also anchor the SPB in the NE through unknown binding interactions with the non-membrane core SPB.
evidence: This is stated as a presumption based on genetic data.

claim: SIM provides a twofold increase in resolution limit compared to conventional widefield and confocal microscopes.
source: SIM provides a twofold increase in this resolution limit (Gustafsson et al., 2008), and we were able to detect two foci of Spc42-GFP that were unresolvable using widefield microscopy (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated with citation and demonstrated in Figure 1C.

claim: Two foci of Spc42-GFP were detected by SIM that were unresolvable using widefield microscopy.
source: SIM provides a twofold increase in this resolution limit (Gustafsson et al., 2008), and we were able to detect two foci of Spc42-GFP that were unresolvable using widefield microscopy (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C.

claim: In most α-factor arrested cells, two Spc42 foci were observed; one focus was significantly brighter than the other.
source: In most α-factor arrested cells, two Spc42 foci were observed; one focus was significantly brighter than the other, a phenotype anticipated for a mother SPB and a satellite that is beginning to assemble (Figure 1A,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The distance between Spc42 foci (225 ± 10 nm) was calculated from the center of the mother SPB to the center of the satellite.
source: The distance between foci (225 ± 10 nm) was calculated from the center of the mother SPB to the center of the satellite so it is greater than the reported length of the extended half-bridge (117 ± 9 nm), which was measured by EM from the edge of SPB to the edge of the satellite (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement from the data.

claim: The distance between Spc42 foci is greater than the reported length of the extended half-bridge (117 ± 9 nm) measured by EM.
source: The distance between foci (225 ± 10 nm) was calculated from the center of the mother SPB to the center of the satellite so it is greater than the reported length of the extended half-bridge (117 ± 9 nm), which was measured by EM from the edge of SPB to the edge of the satellite (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with cited EM data.

claim: Analysis of Spc42-mMaple by PALM reported a distribution of distances between the mother SPB and satellite as 80–280 nm.
source: Analysis of Spc42-mMaple by photo-activated localization microscopy (PALM) reported a distribution of distances between the mother SPB and satellite as 80–280 nm (Seybold et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to another study.

claim: Two closely spaced foci of Tub4-mTurquoise2 were detected at the spindle poles of most cells by SIM.
source: Analysis of Spc42-mMaple by photo-activated localization microscopy (PALM) reported a distribution of distances between the mother SPB and satellite as 80–280 nm (Seybold et al., 2015). By SIM, two closely spaced foci of Tub4-mTurquoise2 were also detected at the spindle poles of most cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: The average distance between Tub4 foci was 157 ± 7 nm, which is similar to the 150 nm height measured from outer to inner plaque by EM.
source: The average distance between foci was 157 ± 7 nm, which is similar to the 150 nm height measured from outer to inner plaque by EM (Byers and Goetsch, 1974; Winey et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement comparison with cited EM data.

claim: SPB substructures (the inner and outer plaques) and duplication intermediates (satellite) can be detected by SIM of endogenously expressed fluorescent fusion proteins.
source: These results show that SPB substructures (the inner and outer plaques) and duplication intermediates (satellite) can be detected by SIM of endogenously expressed fluorescent fusion proteins, which was not possible with previous techniques.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the SIM results.

claim: ImmunoEM analysis of Sfi1 N- and C-termini showed a distribution of gold particles along the length of the bridge with most N-terminal ends located adjacent to the mother SPB or satellite and most C-terminal ends located in the central region of the bridge.
source: ImmunoEM analysis of Sfi1 N- and C-termini showed a distribution of gold particles along the length of the bridge with most N-terminal ends located adjacent to the mother SPB or satellite and most C-terminal ends located in the central region of the bridge.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of immunoEM data.

claim: John Kilmartin proposed that elongation of the half-bridge may occur through end-to-end association of Sfi1 C-termini.
source: Based in part on this and on the observation that Sfi1 is able to form long (60–90 nm) filaments in vitro, John Kilmartin proposed that elongation of the half-bridge may occur through end-to-end association of Sfi1 C-termini; this would generate a free Sfi1 N-terminus that could seed satellite assembly (Figure 2A) (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a proposal with citation.

claim: End-to-end association of Sfi1 C-termini would generate a free Sfi1 N-terminus that could seed satellite assembly.
source: Based in part on this and on the observation that Sfi1 is able to form long (60–90 nm) filaments in vitro, John Kilmartin proposed that elongation of the half-bridge may occur through end-to-end association of Sfi1 C-termini; this would generate a free Sfi1 N-terminus that could seed satellite assembly (Figure 2A) (Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as part of Kilmartin's proposal.

claim: A single Sfi1 focus was observed in 97% of cells treated with α-factor using C-terminally tagged Sfi1 (Sfi1-GFP) in combination with Spc42-mCherry.
source: Using C-terminally tagged Sfi1 (Sfi1-GFP) in combination with Spc42-mCherry, we observed a single Sfi1 focus in 97% of cells treated with α-factor (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2B,C.

claim: Two Sfi1 foci were observed in 62% of N-terminally tagged Sfi1 (GFP-Sfi1) cells arrested under the same conditions.
source: In contrast, two Sfi1 foci were observed in 62% of N-terminally tagged Sfi1 (GFP-Sfi1) cells arrested under the same conditions (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2B,C.

claim: The distance between GFP-Sfi1 foci was 187 ± 1 nm, which is longer than estimates of bridge length obtained from EM studies (117 ± 9 nm).
source: The distance between GFP-Sfi1 foci was 187 ± 1 nm, which is longer than estimates of bridge length obtained from EM studies (117 ± 9 nm; Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement comparison with cited EM data.

claim: Many cells exhibit increased GFP-Sfi1 fluorescence at the distal end near the satellite compared with the proximal end.
source: Unlike Spc42-mCherry intensity, which is greatest at the mother SPB and shows reduced levels at the satellite, many cells exhibit increased GFP-Sfi1 fluorescence at the distal end near the satellite compared with the proximal end (Figure 2B,C), suggesting asymmetry along the Sfi1 filament.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2B,C.

claim: The C-terminus of Sfi1 was noticeably displaced towards the cytoplasmic side of the bridge.
source: The C-terminus of Sfi1 was noticeably displaced towards the cytoplasmic side of the bridge (Figure 2B, merged panels) and the average distance between Spc42-mCherry at the mother SPB and Sfi1-GFP in the 'center' of the bridge is significantly shorter than the distance between Sfi1-GFP and the satellite (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The average distance between Spc42-mCherry at the mother SPB and Sfi1-GFP in the 'center' of the bridge is significantly shorter than the distance between Sfi1-GFP and the satellite.
source: The C-terminus of Sfi1 was noticeably displaced towards the cytoplasmic side of the bridge (Figure 2B, merged panels) and the average distance between Spc42-mCherry at the mother SPB and Sfi1-GFP in the 'center' of the bridge is significantly shorter than the distance between Sfi1-GFP and the satellite (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Newly formed Sfi1 is distinct from Sfi1 existing on the half-bridge from the previous cell cycle.
source: Based on these observations, we hypothesize that newly formed Sfi1 is distinct from Sfi1 existing on the half-bridge from the previous cell cycle and that the new Sfi1 filament is built at an angle relative to the existing Sfi1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the observations.

claim: The new Sfi1 filament is built at an angle relative to the existing Sfi1.
source: Based on these observations, we hypothesize that newly formed Sfi1 is distinct from Sfi1 existing on the half-bridge from the previous cell cycle and that the new Sfi1 filament is built at an angle relative to the existing Sfi1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the observations.

claim: Bridge asymmetries may be important for bridge expansion, contraction, and bending.
source: These asymmetries may be important for bridge expansion, contraction, and bending, which have previously been proposed to facilitate formation and NE insertion of the new SPB (Adams and Kilmartin, 1999, 2000).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation with citations.

claim: SPA-SIM involves the generation of probability profiles depicting the average position of the second SPB component after alignment of many images using Spc42.
source: Conceptually similar to single particle analysis used in many cryoEM studies, SPA-SIM involves the generation of probability profiles depicting the average position of the second SPB component after alignment of many images using Spc42.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the SPA-SIM method.

claim: The C-terminus of Spc42 is above the NE in intermediate layer 2 of the SPB, which is located between the central and outer plaque.
source: Based on EM, the C-terminus of Spc42 is above the NE in intermediate layer 2 of the SPB, which is located between the central and outer plaque; the Spc42 N-terminus is located in the central plaque, which is spaced 10.8 nm from intermediate layer 2 towards the NE (Bullitt et al., 1997; O'Toole et al., 1999; Muller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on cited EM data.

claim: The Spc42 N-terminus is located in the central plaque, which is spaced 10.8 nm from intermediate layer 2 towards the NE.
source: Based on EM, the C-terminus of Spc42 is above the NE in intermediate layer 2 of the SPB, which is located between the central and outer plaque; the Spc42 N-terminus is located in the central plaque, which is spaced 10.8 nm from intermediate layer 2 towards the NE (Bullitt et al., 1997; O'Toole et al., 1999; Muller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated based on cited EM data.

claim: Examination of YFP intensity in aligned images showed a high degree of correlation in the mother-satellite axis, while in the pole axis the ∼15 nm shift in intensity maxima is consistent with the position of the N-terminus in the central plaque and the C-terminus in intermediate layer 2.
source: Examination of YFP intensity in aligned images showed a high degree of correlation in the mother-satellite axis, while in the pole axis the ∼15 nm shift in intensity maxima is consistent with the position of the N-terminus in the central plaque and the C-terminus in intermediate layer 2 (Figure 3A,B; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3A,B and Table 1.

claim: The use of Spc42 enables comparison of positional information between multiple images with high confidence using the alignment methods.
source: These data demonstrate that we have excellent color alignment in our raw images and that the use of Spc42 enables comparison of positional information between multiple images with high confidence using our alignment methods.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the alignment analysis.

claim: Sfi1-GFP is displaced and GFP-Sfi1 is also cytoplasmically shifted relative to Spc42.
source: Not only is Sfi1-GFP displaced, but GFP-Sfi1 is also cytoplasmically shifted relative to Spc42 (Figure 3C–E; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3C-E and Table 1.

claim: The shifts of Sfi1-GFP (29.4 ± 1.4 nm) and GFP-Sfi1 (12.1 ± 1.0 nm) are significantly less than the ∼100 nm resolution achievable by SIM alone.
source: These shifts of 29.4 ± 1.4 nm (Sfi1-GFP) and 12.1 ± 1.0 nm (GFP-Sfi1) are significantly less than the ∼100 nm resolution achievable by SIM alone (Gustafsson et al., 2008), suggesting that our SPA-SIM approach can provide at least a 5–10-fold improvement in intensity distribution localization.
evidence: This is stated as a measurement comparison with cited SIM resolution.

claim: The SPA-SIM approach can provide at least a 5–10-fold improvement in intensity distribution localization.
source: These shifts of 29.4 ± 1.4 nm (Sfi1-GFP) and 12.1 ± 1.0 nm (GFP-Sfi1) are significantly less than the ∼100 nm resolution achievable by SIM alone (Gustafsson et al., 2008), suggesting that our SPA-SIM approach can provide at least a 5–10-fold improvement in intensity distribution localization.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the measurement data.

claim: A 17 ± 2° bend in the extended half-bridge was readily apparent.
source: A 17 ± 2° bend in the extended half-bridge was readily apparent as was the asymmetry between old and new Sfi1 filaments and the increased intensity of GFP-Sfi1 at the satellite (Figures 2D, 3E).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figures 2D and 3E.

claim: The kink in the extended half-bridge occurs in the direction of the pole axis, which is perpendicular to the NE.
source: This kink in the extended half-bridge occurs in the direction of the pole axis, which is perpendicular to the NE.
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: The kink in the extended half-bridge is greater than the natural bend predicted based on the curvature of the NE, which would be ∼7° based on a 1 µm nuclear diameter.
source: It is greater than the natural bend predicted based on the curvature of the NE, which would be ∼7° based on a 1 µm nuclear diameter (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with a calculated value.

claim: Mps3 and Kar1 molecules were distributed along the half-bridge in asynchronous and α-factor arrested cells.
source: Unlike Sfi1, which appeared to form a filament with a distinct polarity, Mps3 and Kar1 molecules were distributed along the half-bridge in asynchronous and α-factor arrested cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; data not shown) (Seybold et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Probability profiles of Mps3-YFP and YFP-Kar1 showed that both proteins are displaced along the pole axis.
source: Probability profiles of Mps3-YFP and YFP-Kar1 showed that both proteins are displaced along the pole axis (Figure 3C,D; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3C,D and Table 1.

claim: Mps3 is primarily at the inner NE face of the half-bridge and Kar1 is primarily cytoplasmic.
source: Previous immunoEM analysis showed that Mps3 is primarily at the inner NE face of the half-bridge and Kar1 is primarily cytoplasmic (Vallen et al., 1992b; Jaspersen et al., 2002), so we have shown distributions according to their proper orientation (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This is stated based on cited immunoEM data.

claim: YFP-Kar1 is more broadly distributed along the mother-satellite axis than Sfi1-GFP (179 ± 3 nm compared to 154 ± 4 nm).
source: Based on the full-width half-maximum (FWHM) values of our Gaussian fits, YFP-Kar1 is more broadly distributed along the mother-satellite axis than Sfi1-GFP (179 ± 3 nm compared to 154 ± 4 nm; Table 1), which was confirmed by inspection of the probability profiles and individual SIM images (Figure 3C,F; data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as a measurement with reference to Table 1 and Figure 3C,F.

claim: The broader distribution of Kar1 along the extended half-bridge may be important for its association with pore components of the SPB.
source: The broader distribution that we observe for Kar1 along the extended half-bridge may be important for its association with pore components of the SPB (discussed below).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation.

claim: N- or C-terminal fusions of fluorescent proteins to CDC31 were lethal when expressed under the endogenous promoter.
source: N- or C-terminal fusions of fluorescent proteins to CDC31 were lethal when expressed under the endogenous promoter; however a cdc31∆::MET-YFP-CDC31 strain was viable and YFP-Cdc31 was detected as one or two foci in most α-factor arrested cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: A cdc31∆::MET-YFP-CDC31 strain was viable and YFP-Cdc31 was detected as one or two foci in most α-factor arrested cells.
source: N- or C-terminal fusions of fluorescent proteins to CDC31 were lethal when expressed under the endogenous promoter; however a cdc31∆::MET-YFP-CDC31 strain was viable and YFP-Cdc31 was detected as one or two foci in most α-factor arrested cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The brighter focus of YFP-Cdc31 (focus 2) was located at a distal region of the bridge interior to the N-terminus of Sfi1.
source: Alignment of images using Spc42-mCherry present in the strain showed that the brighter focus (focus 2) was located at a distal region of the bridge interior to the N-terminus of Sfi1 (Figure 3C–E; Table 1).
